title: Find the root cause, run the job, recommend clearly

say: Find the root cause, run the job well, and recommend clearly.
This is the video for module two of Consulting Fundamentals.
You do not need expensive software. A spreadsheet, a survey tool, a shared folder and a few thinking tools are enough.

say: Draw a process map with the people who actually do the work, not only the manager. Mark how long each step takes and how long work waits. Waiting time is usually where improvements hide.

items: Process map: where does work slow down?
Pareto: which few causes make most problems?

Stakeholder map: who can block or support?

say: A parcel delivery company in Port Harcourt logged 400 complaints in three months. Late delivery 180, wrong address 90, damaged parcels 50, and smaller groups.

say: At kick-off, restate the key question, confirm scope, name one client contact, and hand over a written data request with dates. Then send a short inception note that records it all.

say: Every week, send a five-line update rated green, amber or red. Bad news early is good service. Clients rarely forgive surprises in the final week.

say: Put the answer first. Use Situation, Complication, Question, Answer, then three supporting arguments, each with evidence. This is the pyramid principle.
Give each chart an action title, like: three causes create 80% of complaints.

A strong recommendation says what, who, by when, the cost, and the expected result. Before the meeting, share the main messages privately with key people, so nobody is surprised in front of colleagues.
Check that totals add up and the same figure is identical everywhere. Mark estimates. Ask someone who has not seen the work to tell you the main message.
Interview notes, salaries and customer lists are confidential. Keep them in password-protected folders, share only with people named in the agreement, and never reuse one client's data for another.

panel.heading: Before anything reaches the client
items: Numbers tie out everywhere they appear
Every claim has a source; estimates marked
A second person repeats the main message
Confidential notes in protected folders
Names removed from quotes unless agreed

say: Remember. Match the tool to the question, and look for causes the client can change. Plan in consultant days and report every week. And always lead with the answer.

panel.heading: What to keep from this module
items: Match the tool to the question
Look for causes the client can change
Plan in consultant days; report weekly
Answer first, then arguments and evidence

say: Run a Pareto analysis on at least 30 records and a 5 Whys for the biggest category. Build a workplan in consultant days. Then write a one-page memo with the answer first.
Now continue with the lessons below.
